## Step-by-step solution

**Given information:**
- Prior probability of condition: P(D) = 1/500 = 0.002
- P(no D) = 0.998
- Sensitivity: P(+ | D) = 0.98
- Specificity: P(– | no D) = 0.95, so P(+ | no D) = 0.05 (false positive rate)

**Apply Bayes' theorem:**

$$P(D \mid +) = \frac{P(+|D)\,P(D)}{P(+|D)\,P(D) + P(+|\text{no }D)\,P(\text{no }D)}$$

**Compute numerator:**
P(+|D)·P(D) = 0.98 × 0.002 = 0.00196

**Compute denominator terms:**
- True positives: 0.00196
- False positives: P(+|no D)·P(no D) = 0.05 × 0.998 = 0.0499

Total P(+) = 0.00196 + 0.0499 = 0.05186

**Final calculation:**

$$P(D \mid +) = \frac{0.00196}{0.05186} = 0.037794\ldots = 3.7794\%$$

Rounded to two decimal places: **3.78%**

This illustrates the classic base-rate effect: even with a fairly accurate test (98% sensitivity, 95% specificity), because the condition is rare (0.2% prevalence), most positive results are false positives — only about 1 in 26 people who test positive actually has the condition.
